blocks.content: Line chart (Fig 1) of the percentage of children aged 1–4 years in the USA, 1964–1970, with a history of measles vaccine and/or infection (solid line), vaccine (dash-dot line) and infection (dashed line); y-axis “Percent — Pourcentage”, 0–90. Vaccine and/or infection rises from about 51% in 1965 to about 66% in 1967–1969 and falls to about 61% in 1970; vaccination rises from about 24% in 1964 to about 60% in 1969; infection declines from about 20% to about 7%.

Line chart (Fig 2) of polio immunization among children aged 1–4 years in the USA, 1959–1970; y-axis “Percent — Pourcentage”, 0–90. The share with 3+ IPV and/or 3+ OPV (solid line) rises from about 65% in 1959 to a peak of about 87% in 1964, drops to about 74% in 1965, and declines to about 66% by 1970; the share with no vaccine (dashed line) falls from about 16% to about 10%.

Line chart (Fig 3) of diphtheria–tetanus–pertussis immunization among children aged 1–4 years in the USA, 1962–1970; y-axis “Percent — Pourcentage”, 0–90, x-axis “Year — Année”. The share with 3+ doses (solid line) rises from about 68% in 1962 to about 76–78% from 1964 onward; the share with no vaccine (dashed line) declines from about 14% to about 7%.

Scanned full page (page 174) of a bilingual English–French report, “Immunization Survey — 1970 / Enquête sur les vaccinations — 1970”, on the United States survey, with three line charts for children aged 1–4 years: Fig 1, history of measles vaccine and/or infection, USA 1964–1970; Fig 2, polio immunization, USA 1959–1970; and Fig 3, diphtheria–tetanus–pertussis immunizations, USA 1962–1970. In each chart the immunized share is far above the share with no vaccine or with infection, which declines over time.
